messages:
incident-bot: Pager P1 — router alert: high request drop rate to Dedicated pool dp-42 (us-west-2). Symptoms: 502/504 spikes, significant request blackholing. Auto-escalate to oncall.
anika: acked. I'm on it. pulling metrics now.
mike: seeing the same — router's fallback policy just started routing traffic to dp-42 variant 'gptx-8q' which is incompatible with the pool's runtime; those instances are rejecting frames. logs look like mismatch during kernel selection.
anika: can you paste the exporter output /metrics snippet?
mike: here, last lines from exporter (truncated):
```
# HELP redwood_pool_util Percent util (legacy)
redwood_pool_util 0.03
# HELP pool_util Percent util (new)
pool_util 0.85
```
mike: autoscaler is reading redwood_pool_util but our metrics agent switched to emitting pool_util an hour ago. autoscaler thinks pool is idle -> scaled down -> router sees low capacity -> fallback kicks in -> then router selects wrong variant due to a policy priority shuffle.
anika: oof. so two problems: metrics name changed (autoscaler misread) and router fallback policy picks variant that dp-42 can't handle.
jordan: any customer impact yet? which tenants are affected?
kat: alerting/metrics show increased 429/timeout on a handful of enterprise tenants in us-west-2. Ticket INC-2248 opened by Support. We should correlate requests by customer id.
tess: I'm pulling request traces now — most requests show route fail at the pool handoff stage with error: "variant-mismatch: incompatible-kernel"
anika: mitigation plan: 1) immediately override router to prefer hosted variants for affected routes 2) restart metrics-exporter + patch autoscaler to read pool_util 3) scale dp-42 up manually to absorb inflight 4) follow-up: revert metrics agent change or update autoscaler config. executing now.
mike: +1 on the plan. I'll do the router override — doing a dry run then apply.
mike: run: ```curl -s -X POST "https://console.internal.redwood/api/v1/router/override" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","policy":{"prefer":"hosted","note":"temp-mitigation-1955"}}'``` -> response 200, override applied.
anika: doing scale and exporter restart now:
```
kubectl -n redwood-dedicated rollout restart deployment/metrics-exporter
rcli pool update --pool-id dp-42 --min-instances 4 --force
```
anika: metrics-exporter restarted, new metrics show both names for now. pushing autoscaler config patch to read both metrics keys.
kat: Support notified customers about degraded performance and mitigation steps, added INC-2248 updates. CC: account teams.
tess: after override, error rates dropped ~60% for affected tenants. Some requests still 503 during in-flight failover.
jordan: how about the root cause of the exporter change? was it a deliberate deploy?
mike: looks like a rollout of metrics-agent v2 at 06:12 UTC that switched metric name. change was rolled by infra pipeline but autoscaler config wasn't updated in the same rollout group.
anika: temporary config patch applied to autoscaler to fallback to pool_util if redwood_pool_util missing. pushing PR to infra: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/af3b2
anika: follow-up actions we need tracked in incident ticket:
- permanent autoscaler change to accept both metric names (or stable metric name) [owner: infra]
- postmortem on rollout coordination between metrics agent and autoscaler [owner: eng-oncall]
- review router fallback policy to avoid variant selection that is incompatible with pool capabilities; add variant-compat checks [owner: eng-runtime]
- customer compensation assessment for impacted accounts [owner: customer-success]
mike: leaving a note here — disable automatic fallback-to-dedicated for route /v1/generate while we add variant compat checks. that's already partially covered by override but we should make it explicit in router policy store.
anika: I've added tasks to the console and set a canary to make sure the fix doesn't flip other regions.
sasha: I'm taking over the oncall at 08:00 UTC. what's outstanding that I should pick up during my shift?
anika: handoff to @sasha — current status: router override in place (prefer-hosted), metrics-exporter restarted, autoscaler patched (accepts both keys), dp-42 manually scaled to min 4. Still outstanding: revert or properly roll autoscaler config, add variant-compat guard, confirm no more regressions in us-west-2, liaise with Support for customer follow-ups. ETA for full rollback: ~3-6h.
sasha: ack, taking it. I'll monitor for 2 full scaling cycles and verify pods don't go below min. will also confirm the PR for autoscaler merge.
mike: leaving notes in INC-2248 with timeline and commands run. linking logs and graphs.
kat: Support sent an interim update to impacted customers; CS will await final postmortem before any compensation decisions.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: autoscaler-patch v1.0 -> SUCCESS (build 8721) by mike at 07:22 UTC.
anika: before I drop off, quick postmortem points: prevent single-metric-name drift, add integration test that deploys metrics-agent and autoscaler together in staging, and add router policy unit test for variant compatibility. adding all to P0 postmortem doc.
sasha: thanks @anika, @mike. I'll pick up next steps and ping if we see any regression. tagging incident as active -> handoff complete.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2248 acknowledged. Current severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 (mitigated). Assigned to eng-runtime for follow-up.
